sql.description: One read statement: SELECT, VALUES, TABLE, SHOW, or EXPLAIN of a read query; MySQL and MariaDB also accept DESCRIBE. PostgreSQL requires schema-qualified tables and views. MySQL and MariaDB connections have no default database, so name tables as database.table. System schemas and application routines are permitted; writes and transaction control are rejected.

parameters.description: Ordered JSON values bound separately to placeholders: $1, $2, etc. for PostgreSQL and ? for MySQL and MariaDB. Null means SQL NULL; objects and arrays become JSON text. PostgreSQL infers types from text; use casts such as $1::uuid, and array-text strings for arrays. MySQL and MariaDB bind integers and booleans as integers and other numbers as exact decimal text; use CAST(? AS JSON) for JSON.
